newsitem.title: USA: W.R. Grace operating income up on packing, construction.
newsitem.headline: W.R. Grace operating income up on packing, construction.

text.p: W.R. Grace & Co. said Friday its operating income edged higher in the first quarter, boosted by its packaging and construction products businesses.
Income from continuing operations rose to $46.4 million, or 60 cents a share, in the quarter ended March 31, from $43.6 million, or 44 cents a share, in the year-ago period.
The 1996 quarter results included $20 million in earnings from Grace's Dearborn unit, which has now been sold.
Net income was also reduced by difficult market conditions in the fluid cracking catalyst business, Grace said.

Sales growth, excluding divested businesses, was strong in North America and Latin America, but sales edged down in Europe and Asia Pacific, mainly due to the effect of a stronger dollar, which reduced reported sales by 2.5 percent.

Grace Packaging, a maker of flexible plastic packaging and container sealants, saw pretax income rise 12 percent to $67 million due to a favourable product mix and continuing cost management, it said. Sales rose 3 percent to $489 million.
Sales of packaging for fresh red meat rose in every region, with North America and Latin America both experiencing double-digit growth.
Sales for display films grew in every region, particularly in Asia Pacific and Latin America, Grace said.
Grace Davison, a supplier of catalysts and silica products, saw pretax income tumble 37 percent to $18 million, while sales fell 6 percent to $175 million.

Grace Construction Products, a supplier of concrete additives, cement processing aids, and structural waterproofing and fireproofing products, earned $4 million before taxes, compared with a $4 million loss the prior year. Sales jumped 22 percent to $103 million.
Grace said it expects overall sales to grow by between 6 percent and 7 percent for the year, boosted by packaging and refinery catalyst markets.
The Boca Raton, Fla.-based company's stock rose 12.5 cents to $48.75 on the New York Stock Exchange shortly before midday.
